signature.smime.title: S/MIME
signature.smime.admin_help: E-mails of the wiki are signed with S/MIME when a valid certificate fits the sender address. Recipients then see that the e-mail really comes from the wiki and was not changed on the way.
signature.smime.org_help: For the senders of the wiki (sender and allowed senders in the e-mail settings). Upload a new certificate before the old one expires: from the start of its validity the new one is used automatically.
signature.smime.personal_admin_help: Certificates people uploaded for e-mails sent in their name. You can remove them here, for example when a key is no longer safe.
signature.smime.untrusted: This server does not know the certification authority. Recipients must trust it themselves.
signature.smime.file_help: PKCS#12 (.p12, .pfx) with a password, or PEM with the certificate and an unencrypted private key. At most 256 kB.
signature.smime.password_help: Only to open the file. It is not stored.
signature.smime.label: Label
signature.smime.remove_confirm: Remove the certificate "{name}"? The private key is deleted.
signature.smime.set_mail_signing_help: Outgoing e-mails are signed when a valid certificate fits the sender address.
signature.smime.on_expired: When all certificates of a sender have expired
signature.smime.on_expired_help: Administrators are warned 60, 30, 14, 7 and 1 day before a certificate expires.
signature.smime.set_personal_help: People can upload their own certificate in their profile. E-mails with their address as sender are then signed with it.
signature.smime.set_seal: Seal signature evidence with the certificate of the organisation
signature.smime.set_seal_help: In addition to the seal of the wiki. A valid certificate of the organisation marked "Also seal signature evidence" is used. It can also be checked with OpenSSL.
signature.smime.mine_help: With your own certificate the wiki signs e-mails sent with your address as the sender, for example from workflows.
signature.smime.mine_legal: Note: for this the private key is stored encrypted on the server. This proves the sender; it is not an electronic signature under your sole control. Every use is logged. You can remove the certificate at any time.
signature.smime.mine_addresses: The certificate must contain one of your confirmed addresses: {emails}
signature.smime.expiry_soon_body: The S/MIME certificate for {emails} expires on {date}. Upload a new one in time.
signature.smime.expiry_tomorrow_body: The S/MIME certificate for {emails} expires on {date}. Upload a new one now.
signature.smime.expired_body: The S/MIME certificate for {emails} expired on {date}.
signature.smime.expiry_after_unsigned: After it expires, e-mails of this sender are sent unsigned.
signature.smime.expiry_after_hold: After it expires, e-mails of this sender are held in the outbox until a valid certificate is available.
perm.signature.smime.manage_help: Upload and remove the certificates of the organisation and change the S/MIME settings.
